title: I'm building a life sim with AI coding agents. Here's the first look at SimGoodie.
author: alexid95
selftext:
I'm Alexander, the solo developer of SimGoodie, a life sim I'm building in Unity in my free time. The ambition is the character depth I loved in The Sims 2 with an open world inspired by The Sims 3. This is still an early build.

I use Claude Code alongside other coding agents for implementation and UI work. I break changes into scoped OpenSpec tasks and use a separate review pass. There is also a headless simulation lab for running gameplay scenarios over simulated days, so I can check how systems behave together.

Game Log #2 gets into a concrete example: a floor could look fully covered while giving a character nowhere to walk. The build preview, finished geometry and simulation all need to agree. The full walkthrough leaves in the second-floor problems and blocked interactions, so it shows where the game actually stands.

The attached clip is a first look at the current game. There isn't a public playable build yet.

Game Log #2 with screenshots and the full video: [https://simgoodie.com/devlog/the-house-needs-a-floor-before-it-needs-a-reputation](https://simgoodie.com/devlog/the-house-needs-a-floor-before-it-needs-a-reputation)

For others using agents on games with connected systems, what has helped you catch regressions between building, navigation and character simulation?
